observations: Journal evidence: the CG-C1 loser records outcome reused_before_download with reason 'gap_closed_by_concurrent' — direct proof the in-lock re-check (not the pre-lock step-2 shortcut) is the mechanism completing the loser with fetch=0.

Lock-wait boundedness proven under real contention: reviewer probe held the lock in thread A (1.5s) while thread B contended with timeout_seconds=0.3 -> CatalogOperationLockedError('timed out serializing catalog lock acquisition') after ~0.6s; no hang. execute() converts it to a failed result (reason close_gap_lock_timeout: ...) that callers may retry (DL-09-safe).

CG-C4 as shipped does NOT exercise lock contention: both executes are sequential (the first finishes before the second starts), so it only re-tests the rerun-dedupe path; the bounded-timeout behavior it names was verified by the reviewer probe instead. Recommend a contention-based CG-C4 follow-up.

CG-C1 uses two THREADS rather than the plan's two subprocesses; msvcrt.locking byte-range locks do serialize same-process threads (fetch==1 proves it) and the same primitive is used cross-process, so the single-flight property holds at the file-lock level regardless of caller topology.

Docstring/code mismatch in _is_retryable_staging_error: its docstring and IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_FC804.md design say provider_unavailable is retryable, but the code returns False for RuntimeError('provider unavailable...'). No code path raises that RuntimeError today (provider_unavailable is a GapPlan status field — gap_plan.py/acquisition.py — not an exception), so the branch is dead code with a stale docstring: no live-path impact, and the receipt's OPS-02 claim (AdapterProcessError.retryable only) is accurate as implemented.

DL-02 authorization rejection still short-circuits before retry classification: the 'download not authorized' check runs on every attempt before _is_retryable_staging_error, preserving FC-801 semantics (code read + 7-test FC-801 regression green).

Retry loop hygiene: on final failure (exhausted or non-retryable) the staging dir is cleaned via _cleanup_staging(staged_request.request_id) — the STAGING request's per-candidate id, matching FC-803 REAL-FIX-3; failures are journaled (outcome failed, error_type set); rejections (stale_gap_hash, DL-02, stage_status) are not journaled, consistent with pre-FC-804 behavior.
